text:
sara: Heads-up, saw a weird oscillation in prefix-cache hit-rate on prod this morning around 08:42 UTC. p50 latency jumped ~40ms and hit-rate dropped from 86% -> 58% for ~6m. Rolling window shows correlation with larger batch sizes coming from continuous-batcher.
kevin: ugh. any obvious error logs or OOMs?
sara: no OOMs. RT profiler shows a lot of KV misses and repeated cache key churn. stack traces point to cache_keyer generating variable keys for the same prompt prefix when batching mixes user tokens. snippet: 
```
cache_key = f"{model}:{prefix_hash}:{user_shard}:{kv_version}"
# observed user_shard flipping between 0/1 for same request group
```
liam: flipping user_shard? that suggests batching composition is interleaving contexts and our keying uses ephemeral shard derived from request_hash_mod_2. When batcher groups by arrival time, distribution skews and shards bounce.
devon: can you paste the batch composition sample? i want to see sizes + homogeneity.
sara: here's one capture (trimmed):
```
batch_id: b-2026-03-17-084200
members: [user: A, prompt_len: 120], [user: B, prompt_len: 8], [user: C, prompt_len: 120], [user: D, prompt_len: 6]
continuous_batch_window_ms: 12
resulting_batch_size: 64
avg_prefix_overlap: low
```
liam: that explains it. mixing long + short prefixes reduces prefix overlap so KV reuse plummets, but continuous batcher's default policy prefers higher fill. So tradeoff: lower unit cost vs lower cache hit-rate -> higher per-token exec because of extra MV cache misses.
kevin: do we have perf numbers for dropping window to 4ms?
sara: quick A/B we ran on canary: window=4ms => hit-rate 79%, p50 latency back to baseline, but overall throughput dropped ~6% (reduction in batching efficiency).
liam: that matches expectations. Also we should consider stronger cache key normalization: remove user_shard from primary key and move it as routing hint. then we only key on canonicalized prefix text + model + kv_version. that would avoid shard churn but may reduce isolation for per-tenant caching.
devon: we can't completely drop tenant from key for multi-tenant Dedicated customers. compromise: prefix_key = canonical_prefix_hash + tenant_id_namespace (coarse), not per-request shard. or use two-level cache: global prefix cache + tenant overlay.
kevin: two-level cache is interesting but more memory. What's fastest to deploy to mitigate regression?
sara: short-term: reduce continuous-batcher window to 6ms for affected region + add jitter to queueing to avoid synchronized bursts. mid-term: key normalization change (prefix-only hash) + fallback for Dedicated tenants.
liam: also saw KV warmup lag when switching models after rollouts. we could opportunistically prefetch KV for top N hottest prefixes when new model version becomes primary. cheap warmup: sample top-1k prefixes from recent traffic and push into cache during rollout.
kevin: how safe is prefetch for privacy? must ensure we don't leak user private prefixes across tenants. prefetch must be tenant-scoped.
devon: agreed. tenant-scoped + TTL short (e.g., 5m) during rollouts.
infra-bot: deployplan created: PR#4823 -> reduce batcher.window_ms to 6 for region eu-west-1 (canary first) ; add queue_jitter config = true. CI e2e perf will run.
sara: i ran a micro-profiling trace showing kernel selection thrash after cache miss storm: kernel-switching overhead ~2.8ms per request due to cold kernel warms. log: 
```
[perf] cache_miss_rate: 0.42 -> kernel_sel_latency: 3.1ms -> token_exec_latency: +12ms
```
liam: can we mitigate kernel warm by pinning a hot kernel for short windows when batcher sees frequent model swaps? maybe keep last-used kernel hot for 30s.
devon: would increase GPU memory pressure but could be toggled by runtime heuristics.
kevin: action items?
sara: 1) canary change batcher.window_ms=6 in eu-west-1 (devon) 2) enable queue_jitter flag for continuous-batcher (kevin) 3) implement lightweight key-normalization (liam) 4) add prefetch hook to rollouts for top-1k prefixes (sara) 5) dashboard: track batch_size distribution vs prefix-hit-rate (devon)
liam: i'll prototype key-normalization today, PR by EOD. will keep tenant namespace but collapse ephemeral shard.
kevin: i'll flip the jitter flag and watch canary. infra-bot will post CI results. :thumbsup:
sara: thanks. if we see oscillation again, we should capture a batch dump + kv key hashes and also save continuous-batcher trace to /var/logs/batcher/ for offline repro.
devon: acked, starting canary in 2m.
infra-bot: canary started at 1729988800, traffic ramp 5% -> 20% over 3m. monitoring endpoints: /internal/metrics/batcher and /internal/metrics/prefix_cache
sara: perfect. i'll monitor hit-rate and p50. will post updates in this thread. :eyes:
